text:
For a **typical electric blanket**, I’d choose the **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2**. Its 1,024 Wh battery is estimated to run a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours—enough for an eight-hour night with some margin, though actual runtime depends on the blanket’s settings and how often its thermostat cycles ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)).

Check your blanket’s label before buying: a blanket drawing around **100 W** could use roughly 800 Wh over eight hours, while one drawing **260 W continuously** could need about **2,600 Wh of station capacity** after losses. For that higher-draw case, the [Jackery HomePower 3000](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) is estimated to last about 9.5 hours.

Keep the power station off the bed, and plug the blanket directly into its outlet.
